LESSON: NON-VERBAL CUES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: SPORTS - APPRECIATING TALENTS Suggested Vocabulary to be signed competition, che
Topic 1.3: Non-verbal cues
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Non-verbal cues, part of SPORTS - APPRECIATING TALENTS Suggested Vocabulary to be signed competition, che in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to listen carefully and observe keenly? 2. How can we become better listeners and observers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Non-verbal cues together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Articulating signs clearly as learners make short signed speeches.

• Learning to learn: Self-discipline as learners practise saying as they sign tongue twisters and finger fumblers.

• Self-Efficacy: as learners pick out target letter sounds from poems or stories.

Values:
Responsibility: Determination as learners, individually, make a three-minute signed speech.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to relate the theme; sports to their learning in Creative Arts.
